response: Yes, type 1 diabetes mellitus can affect the Achilles tendon response to a 10 km run. Research suggests that individuals with type 1 diabetes may experience altered Achilles tendon properties, such as reduced stiffness and increased thickness, after exercise, which may be related to changes in blood glucose levels and inflammation. However, more studies are needed to fully understand the impact of type 1 diabetes on Achilles tendon response to exercise.
